nodes.description: Public state variable 'uint entropy' that stores the accumulated XOR entropy and is both read and written by getRandomNumber, acting as the contract's pseudo-random seed.

Public function getRandomNumber() that mutates the entropy state variable with a blockhash-derived value and returns it; exposed to any external caller with no access control and no randomness commitment.

Statement 'entropy ^= uint(blockhash(entropy % block.number));' - an unsafe entropy/randomness computation that derives its value from blockhash and block.number, both miner-influenceable, and directly writes the result into persistent state, enabling prediction/manipulation of the returned 'random' number.

edges.reason: The current value of state variable 'entropy' is read as the left operand of the XOR and as the mod operand (entropy % block.number) inside the computation.
The unsafe XOR-with-blockhash computation writes its result back into the 'entropy' state variable, persistently updating the seed used by future calls.
Invoking getRandomNumber() unconditionally executes the entropy ^= blockhash(...) statement as the first instruction of the function body.

Any external caller may invoke getRandomNumber() and thereby read and mutate the 'entropy' state variable without any authorization check, so the state change is reachable by arbitrary msg.sender addresses.
The function's return value is the post-update value of the 'entropy' state variable, flowing from state storage back into the function's return path.
